title: Selective Query-Guided Debiasing for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval

problems.name: Multi-Moment, Compositional, and Complex Query Grounding
problems.evidence_sentence: Selective Query-Guided Debiasing for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval Video moment retrieval (VMR) aims to localize target moments in untrimmed videos pertinent to a given textual query.

problems.name: Dataset, Benchmark, and Evaluation Mismatch
problems.evidence_sentence: Existing retrieval systems tend to rely on retrieval bias as a shortcut and thus, fail to sufficiently learn multi-modal interactions between query and video.

problems.name: Scalability and Corpus-Level Retrieval
problems.evidence_sentence: Selective Query-Guided Debiasing for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval Video moment retrieval (VMR) aims to localize target moments in untrimmed videos pertinent to a given textual query.

methods.name: Object/Event/Spatio-Temporal Modules
methods.evidence_sentence: This retrieval bias stems from learning frequent co-occurrence patterns between query and moments, which spuriously correlate objects (e.g., a pencil) referred in the query with moments (e.g., scene of writing with a pencil) where the objects frequently appear in the video, such that they converge into biased moment predictions.
